green: Commerce - from a product click to an order or a failed payment
Unique and permanent. Quoted in the technical document, in every test result and in every status call until the project closes. Never renumber one.
column3: The requirement or requirements from the BRD that this solution answers. STD means every implementation needs this and nobody asked for it.
column4: The part of the site or the mechanism. Groups solutions that share a shape.
column5: What is being solved, in one line, written so a business reader recognises their own request.
column6: The variable or event that will carry the value. (M) is merchandising. (n) is numeric. (M n) is a numeric merchandising event.
column7: The report name the variable will carry. Agreed here, because this is what the business will see in Workspace.
column8: The format and a real example value. Enough that a developer and an analyst read the same meaning.
column10: How the value is populated: a data layer object set by the site, or code inside the tag manager.
column11: Page load, event based or direct call.
column12: The rule name in the tag manager. It matches this exactly, including case.
column13: Page load = the page condition. Event based = the element. Direct call = the identifier string.
column14: The data element that holds this value. One element per data layer object, never the raw path inside a rule.
column15: Instructions to the site developer. This is the only column they need to read. Everything they must populate, and the order it must happen in.
column16: The product objects this solution needs, listed separately because eleven solutions share them.
column17: Where custom code is required. The code itself is on the Custom Code sheet.

column8: Data layer object or tool code

column4: A product is clicked on a listing page
column13: Update the product objects for the clicked product, then call _satellite.track('product_click'). Populate the product objects first. A direct call fired before the objects are set will send an empty product.

column7: Category Listing, Search Results, Room Set, Recently Viewed
Category and product ID only. No price on a click.

column4: A product detail page is viewed
column13: The product page is server rendered but the product objects are filled by a later script, so the page load rule can fire before they exist. Set the product objects, then call _satellite.track('product_view').

column7: Search, Category Listing, Room Set, Recommendation, External
In Stock, Out of Stock, Made to Order
Adobe reserved event. Counts a product detail view.

column4: A product is added to the cart from the product page
column13: Set the cart source to Product Page, update the product objects with the chosen colour and quantity, then call _satellite.track('cart_add'). Quantity is the quantity being added, not the quantity now in the cart.

column7: Product Page, Quick View, Room Set, Wishlist, Reorder

column4: A product is added to the cart from the quick view overlay, without leaving the listing
column13: The same rule serves this solution. Set the cart source to Quick View, update the product objects, then call _satellite.track('cart_add'). The overlay does not change the page, so the page objects stay as they are.

column4: A product is removed from the cart
column13: Update the product objects to hold only the product being removed, then call _satellite.track('cart_remove'). Do not send the whole cart.

Populate the product objects with every product in the cart as an array, then call _satellite.track('cart_view'). Each product needs its own entry. One entry holding several IDs will report as a single product that does not exist.
